name: California

agency.name: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

overview: CDFW issues elk, pronghorn, Nelson bighorn sheep and premium deer tags through one Big Game Drawing under a modified preference point system: each hunt's quota is split between a preference-point drawing and a random draw-by-choice drawing (deer 90/10, apprentice deer 50/50, elk, pronghorn and bighorn sheep 75/25 for quotas of four or more). The 2026 application period ran April 15 - June 2, 2026, with results on or around June 15; 2027 dates are not yet published. Applicants earn one point per species when unsuccessful and lose all points for a species when drawn (deer: when drawn for their first choice), while other deer tags (A, B and most D zones), bear tags and wild turkey hunting are over the counter.

species.drawSystemSummary: Premium deer tags (the C zones, the X zones, D12, D14, D17 and the special archery, muzzleloader, late-season and apprentice hunts) are issued in the Big Game Drawing under a modified preference point system: 90% of each quota goes to first-choice applicants in preference-point order and 10% (one tag when the quota is under 10) in a random draw-by-choice round; unsuccessful applicants' second and then third choices are then drawn at random for any tags left. Apprentice deer hunts split 50% preference / 50% random. Party applications (up to six hunters) use the unrounded average of members' points.
species.residentNote: Applicants earn one deer point when not drawn for their first-choice premium hunt (or by applying with code PD) and lose all deer points when drawn for their first choice. Points are reduced to zero after five consecutive years without applying.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents apply in the same drawing; CDFW's drawing statistics do not separate residents and nonresidents. 2026-27 nonresident first or second deer tag/application: $377.35. Unsuccessful nonresidents may request a refund of the difference from the resident application fee.
species.otcSummary: Deer tags for the A zone, B zones (B1-B6) and D zones D3-5, D6, D7, D8, D9, D10, D11, D13, D15, D16 and D19, plus several archery hunts, are unrestricted (issued on request until the zone quota fills). Leftover premium deer tags are sold first-come, first-served from July 2 at 8:00 a.m.

keyDates.note: All deer tag holders must report by January 31 of the license year, hunted or not; late or missing reports carry a $21.60 non-reporting fee.

species.drawSystemSummary: Elk tags are issued only in the Big Game Drawing, one hunt choice per application, under the modified preference point system: a quota of one tag is drawn at random, two tags split one preference / one random, three tags two / one, and four or more award 75% by preference points and the rest at random. CDFW runs the random draw-by-choice round first, then the preference-point round. Applicants earn one point when unsuccessful and lose all elk points when they receive an elk tag.
species.residentNote: Up to two residents may apply as a party. One elk tag per person per year (Private Lands Management tags excepted).
species.nonresidentNote: Only one nonresident may be drawn for an elk or pronghorn tag annually, and nonresidents cannot apply as a party. 2026-27 nonresident elk tag: $1,871.80.
species.otcSummary: None: there are no over-the-counter elk tags (SHARE and Private Lands Management tags are issued outside the Big Game Drawing).

species.drawSystemSummary: Pronghorn tags are issued only in the Big Game Drawing, one hunt choice per application, under the modified preference point system: a quota of one tag is drawn at random, two tags split one preference / one random, three tags two / one, and four or more award 75% by preference points and the rest at random (random round first, then the preference round). Applicants earn one point when unsuccessful and lose all pronghorn points when they receive a tag.
species.residentNote: Up to two residents may apply as a party. One pronghorn tag per person per year (Private Lands Management tags excepted).
species.nonresidentNote: Only one nonresident may be drawn for an elk or pronghorn tag annually, and nonresidents cannot apply as a party. 2026-27 nonresident pronghorn tag: $628.85.
species.otcSummary: None: pronghorn tags are issued only through the Big Game Drawing (Private Lands Management tags excepted).

species.drawSystemSummary: Nelson (desert) bighorn sheep ram tags are issued only in the Big Game Drawing, one hunt choice per application and no party applications, under the modified preference point system: a quota of one tag is drawn at random, two tags split one preference / one random, three tags two / one, and four or more award 75% by preference points (random round first). A hunter may hold one California bighorn sheep tag in a lifetime; not more than 10% of tags go to nonresidents each year.
species.residentNote: Applicants must be 16 or older on July 1 and must never have drawn a California bighorn sheep tag. Drawn hunters must attend a mandatory in-person orientation.
species.nonresidentNote: Not more than 10 percent of bighorn sheep tags are awarded to nonresidents each year. 2026-27 nonresident bighorn sheep tag: $2,072.75.
species.otcSummary: None: bighorn sheep tags come only from the Big Game Drawing (plus fundraising tags).

species.drawSystemSummary: No drawing: bear tags are sold over the counter (online, license agents, CDFW offices). The season closes on December 27 or earlier once 1,700 bears (archery season included) have been reported taken; CDFW counted 803 as of October 27, 2026.
species.otcSummary: Resident bear tag $62.90, nonresident $397.60 (2026-27). CDFW's bear page says licensed hunters 12 or older may buy two bear tags per license year (the second tag was adopted by the Fish and Game Commission in April 2026); daily bag one bear.

keyDates.label: Unsuccessful 2026 bear tag report card due
keyDates.note: Report cards for unsuccessful tags are due February 1 of the license year; successful hunters report immediately.

species.drawSystemSummary: No drawing for the general seasons: wild turkey needs a California hunting license plus an Upland Game Bird Validation (not required under a Junior Hunting License); there is no turkey tag. Spring limit one bearded turkey per day, three per season combined; fall one either-sex per day, two per season.
species.otcSummary: Upland Game Bird Validation $25.41 (2026-27). CDFW also lists Special Hunts and SHARE Program hunts on its upland game page; those are not covered here.

coverage.notes: Hunts per draw year: 2022: 87, 2023: 88, 2024: 84, 2025: 82, 2026: 82. Counts are CDFW's for all applicants combined (no resident/nonresident split). Preference-point-only applicants (not in rows): 2022: 12,925, 2023: 13,120, 2024: 12,797, 2025: 11,552, 2026: 12,673. Applicants by point value are in each row's note; CDFW does not publish tags drawn by point level, so there is no byPoints. Rows are premium deer hunts only (zone, archery, general late-season, muzzleloader and apprentice hunts); applicants are first-choice applicants. Drawn (first-choice applicants awarded a tag), odds and minPoints (lowest point value drawn in the preference drawing) come from the deer drawing summary in the next year's Big Game Hunting Digest, so 2026 rows have no drawn counts yet. 2024 hunts A19, A20, A21 and A24 have no drawn counts because CDFW's 2024 summary rows for those codes do not match the drawing-statistics PDF. The 2025 general late-season 16-23 point part (DocumentID 242664) prints a preference-point-only row that disagrees with the other parts, so 2025 general late-season hunts carry no point breakdown.
